explanation: Viruses are infectious agents associated with a wide variety of diseases in plants, animals, and humans. They feature a non-cellular construction and can possess either a DNA or RNA genome. Because they can acquire mutations, they are able to evolve. However, they are not considered living organisms because they do not have a metabolism and cannot respond to environmental stimuli. To replicate, they must infect a host cell and exploit its cellular machinery.

questions.q: Which of the following biological features is NOT characteristic of viruses according to the overview?
opts: Possession of a DNA or RNA genome
Ability to replicate independently without a host cell
questions.exp: Viruses require the machinery of the host cell they infect in order to replicate; they cannot replicate independently.

questions.q: What primary reasons are given for why viruses are not considered living?
opts: They are too small to be seen with light microscopes and contain RNA.
They do not have a metabolism and cannot respond to stimuli.
They lack any genetic material and cannot mutate.
They are unable to cause disease in plant and animal tissues.
questions.exp: Viruses are not considered living because they lack their own metabolism and cannot respond to external stimuli.
